Definition: from G1537 and G1325; to give forth, i.e. (specially) to lease:--let forth (out).
BiblicalUsage: To let out is to lease, to hand over a vineyard to tenants, and the Gospels tell the same parable with this word. A householder plants a vineyard, hedges it, and lets it out to husbandmen, and when he sends servants for the fruit, they beat one, kill another, and stone another. The tenants forget the vineyard is not theirs, and the parable ends with the vineyard given to others who will render the fruit.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe everything I have is leased from God, because the vineyard was never the tenants', and neither is my life. I hold that the fruit He asks for is His by right, and I want to render it gladly.
